intro.data: A process turns one thing into another. Both machines in your toolkit have the SAME type — messy spreadsheet → table — so the type alone can't tell you which is right. Only what each one DOES can: the Parser makes the clean table the goal wants, the Shredder makes a shredded mess. The test case below is the requirement (messy spreadsheet → clean table); bring the machine that meets it onto the board and wire it, leaving the other in the tray.
intro.alchemy: A process turns one material into another. Both apparatuses have the SAME type — ore → ingot — so the type alone can't tell you which is right. Only what each one DOES can: the Smelter makes the pure ingot the goal wants, the Crusher makes a cracked one. The test case below is the requirement (ore → pure ingot); bring the apparatus that meets it onto the board, leaving the other in the tray.
intro.spellcraft: A working turns one essence into another. Both runes have the SAME type — spark → flame — so the type alone can't tell you which is right. Only what each one DOES can: Ignition makes the steady flame the goal wants, Smother makes a sputtering one. The test case below is the requirement (spark → steady flame); bring the rune that meets it onto the board, leaving the other in the tray.
intro.abstract: A morphism turns one object into another. Both machines have the SAME type, A → B, so the type cannot tell them apart — only behavior can. The test case is the requirement: a ↦ b. f meets it; g sends a ↦ b′ and fails. 'Correct' means nothing more than meeting that requirement — there is no other reason b beats b′. Place f and wire it from the input.

goal.data: Place and wire the machine whose behavior turns the messy spreadsheet into the clean table the test case requires (not the shredded mess).
goal.alchemy: Place and wire the apparatus whose behavior turns the ore into the pure ingot the test case requires (not the cracked one).
goal.spellcraft: Place and wire the rune whose behavior turns the spark into the steady flame the test case requires (not the sputtering one).
goal.abstract: Both machines are A → B; place and wire the one whose behavior meets the test case a ↦ b (f), not a ↦ b′ (g).

afterSuccess.data: You watched the messy spreadsheet become a clean table. Both machines were the same type, but only one behaved the way you wanted — a process is defined by what it does, not just what it connects.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You watched the raw ore become a pure ingot. Both apparatuses were the same type, but only one behaved the way you wanted — a process is defined by what it does.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You watched the wild spark become a steady flame. Both runes were the same type, but only one behaved the way you wanted — a working is defined by what it does.
afterSuccess.abstract: The input became the goal value. Same-typed morphisms can do different things; a morphism is defined by its behavior.

reveal.summary: The things being transformed are objects; the process between them is an arrow, or morphism. Two morphisms with the same source and target can still behave differently.
reveal.moreFormal: A morphism f: A → B has one source and one target. Knowing its type (A → B) is not the same as knowing what it does.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: f: (input: A) => B — two functions with the same signature can compute different things.
